entries.claim: The new paragraph says 'what the project already has enters the design only at the spine step', which contradicts section 4 ('The design folder', line 307). That section has the brief read `docs/design/` and any folder the dump points to. PLAN-6 line 28 keeps that intent: docs/design reaches the spine only through the brief's quotes.
entries.failure_scenario: Take a project under Cadence (`.planning/PROJECT.md` present) that also has `docs/design/`, or a dump that points to a folder of existing notes, and run `/seldon <dump>`. Section 2 now tells the model that nothing the project already has enters before the spine. Section 4 tells it to read `docs/design/` for the judgment and the brief. A model that follows the broader new sentence skips the design notes, and the brief loses the quotes section 10 requires. No case seeds Cadence files together with `docs/design/`, so the conflict is untested. The cadence-dump run still globbed `docs/design/**`, so this has not been seen to fail.

entries.claim: The pattern 'Recommended path:[\s*_`]*fast path' with flag i has no line anchors. It also accepts newlines and bold or code markup between the words, so it passes when the line-of-its-own, plain-text recommendation that case.yaml and PLAN-2's must-be-true claim is missing.
entries.failure_scenario: The last message is 'I think **Recommended path:** fast path makes sense here, since...', or it puts 'Recommended path:' and 'fast path' on separate lines. Both break SKILL.md section 6 ('on a line of its own ... plain text with no bold or other markup'), but the grader matches either one and the case scores 1.00. The 1.00 run's line-of-its-own property was confirmed only by the executor reading the trace by hand, not by the grader.
